text: For the singles who had wanted to go overseas for egg freezing in the past two years, they could not and their eggs' quality and quantity would have declined.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: While immigration helps to moderate the impact of ageing and the low birth rates in our citizen population, it is by no means a silver bullet to tackle our longer-term demographic challenges.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Couples who have wanted to seek cheaper IVF procedure or Pre-implantation Genetic Screening (PGS) procedure overseas would also have difficulties doing so with the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: How is MOH helping Singaporeans with the total fertility health as part of their parenthood journey?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Mr Chairman, during the Budget debate, I spoke about the increased prevalence of patients with chronic diseases and sought clarifications from MOH on the ways that can better address this trend.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Given that our resident population will continue to age, it is inevitable for our healthcare needs and costs to rise.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: To mitigate the costs of healthcare on individuals, especially long-term burden of chronic diseases, I believe that we need to empower individuals to understand our own health, both in the prevention and prompt management at the onset of common chronic diseases like high blood pressure, diabetes and high cholesterol as well as long-term management and disease control.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: To reduce such cost burden especially on our seniors, it is important to increase education to at-risk groups with customised and relatable content, enable screening for early diagnosis and support long-term management to prevent complications from chronic diseases.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I acknowledge that the efforts to reach out and enable more individuals to manage their own health, if solely placed on our healthcare professionals, will increase their already stretched workloads without more supportive tools provided.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: (In Malay):   Last year, MOH set up the Minority Community Outreach (MCO) working group to improve health for minority communities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: These health issues need to be addressed with care and strategically, taking into account factors, such as cultural differences.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Since then, we have seen several innovative campaigns and programmes, such as Yok Jalan Amal organised by M3@Jurong in Jurong, which received encouraging response.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: Besides physical health and diet, other issues such as mental health have also captured the interest of the community, especially among the youth and elderly.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Chairman, I spoke on adult immunisation last year and, this year, I will again broach this topic.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Getting vaccinated has been a buzzword since the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic and we have seen so much effort put in by governments and health authorities globally.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: In Singapore, we have been very lucky and very successful in our vaccination exercise during this pandemic and we are pushing harder for the younger Singaporeans now to get themselves vaccinated.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Vaccination is important, not just for this pandemic, but for many other diseases.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Most adult Singaporeans would have been more familiar with Influenza vaccine and perhaps also hepatitis B, measles, mumps and rubella.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Eleven diseases were identified, namely, Influenza, pneumococcal diseases, human papillomavirus, tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis, mumps, measles, hepatitis B and varicella, which is the chickenpox virus.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The question is how many adult Singaporeans have kept up with their vaccinations according to this schedule?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: What is MOH's plan to encourage more adults to keep their vaccinations up-to-date to protect themselves?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Even in this House, I am sure many Members have not heard about this particular programme, let alone be up-to-date for the vaccinations.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of preventive health through vaccination.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: In Singapore, we have a well-developed childhood immunisation programme.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Adult Singaporeans should be encouraged to get their immunisations updated periodically to protect themselves against diseases.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Why is the adult vaccination schedule not given more limelight?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Can the Government make it more comprehensive as well as easily accessible and affordable and promote it more?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Then this would definitely encourage more to consider vaccination.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.05 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 2.48 pm until 3.05 pm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, our hospitals, healthcare workers and GP clinics continue to work under pressure as a result of the Omicron wave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Individuals who are not fully vaccinated are more likely to be hospitalised, to require oxygen supplementation, be admitted into ICU care and die.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As the unvaccinated are at a higher risk of infection and becoming seriously ill, Vaccination-differentiated Safe Management Measures (VDS) have been put in place to protect this group of individuals while allowing the fully vaccinated to resume more social and economic activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Leong Mun Wai, I feel, has cherry-picked the data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: He is advocating on behalf of individuals who have not been vaccinated; that is quite reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I think he should have a proper understanding of the effectiveness of vaccinations as the most effective intervention that we have in our COVID-19 fight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And each of these may require admission to ICU, certainly, admission to hospital and have the potential to be fatal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, you can see that the infection-related complications are at least 10 times more frequent than any side effects from the vaccine; and most of the side effects of the vaccine are short-term, temporary and do not have any long-term consequences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These infection-related complications are much more frequent, potentially more severe as compared to vaccine-related adverse events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And the odds are clear, every case of MIS-C and myocarditis is one too many.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I think Mr Leong needs to weigh up both sides of the risk.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Once the Omicron wave has subsided, we will be in a better position to ease our safe management measures further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I understand that Ms Sylvia Lim is interested about the access to and approval for ART test kits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The key considerations when approving ART kits for public health use in Singapore are to ensure that the kits, when used as a self-test, are sufficiently sensitive in detecting COVID-19 infection, easy to use and affordable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The process for approving locally-produced ART kits to meet quality standards is quite clear.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is not more stringent than for foreign-produced kits and is made known to all interested manufacturers and importers who have enquired about ART kits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has made available the Pandemic Special Access Route (PSAR) for expedited registration of ART kits to be used for public health use as directed by MOH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Only ART kits that meet the quality standards of MOH are invited by HSA to apply for PSAR.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And this PSAR route requires significantly fewer clinical samples than the full registration route as MOH will continue to monitor the performance of these kits as they are deployed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There have been instances where local manufacturers could not meet the quality standards, but this should not be misrepresented as an unclear process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have been told what else they need to do to meet the quality standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Lower-income households can already apply through Social Service Offices and Family Service Centres for free kits supplied by MOH.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH also provides free kits for individuals on mandatory Rostered Routine Testing (RRT) at the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Those on Protocols 1, 2, 3 also have access to free ART kits via the ART vending machines located island-wide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will be doing more to support the mental well-being of our citizens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our local study "Growing up in Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes" (GUSTO) found that the mental well-being of the mother during pregnancy can affect the brain development of the foetus, resulting in vulnerability to mood or anxiety disorders later in life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, KKH and NUH will increase their antenatal and postnatal mental health screening for more mothers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will allow pregnant women with depressive symptoms to be identified earlier and allows treatment during both pregnancy and motherhood to occur earlier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Studies have shown that screen time during early childhood could have a negative association with later cognition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We agree with Ms Ng Ling Ling that more can be done to support parents in calibrating the exposure of their children to screen time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Practical guides and resources will be developed for parents to help them develop healthy screen time habits in their children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We need to encourage healthy lifestyle habits from as early as possible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being comprises members from over 30 organisations and we met regularly to review the population’s mental health needs, discuss identified gaps and develop some preliminary recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The focus of these efforts are challenges that cut across the responsibilities of several agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about our progress.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: One of the issues identified is the need for better coordination between the health and social service sectors for individuals with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Another clear need is to increase community touchpoints for access to mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will better leverage existing health and social care settings for service delivery and also equip our frontline workers with skills to identify persons with mental health needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are now refining the recommendations for each of these areas and we will be seeking the public’s views in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: After that, a national strategy and an action plan on mental health will be developed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also study Dr Shahira’s suggestion to set up a mental well-being office.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Part of our efforts have been the Youth Mental Well-being (YMWB) Network, launched in February 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This aims to implement initiatives to enhance the mental well-being of youths, mobilise the enthusiasm of youth volunteers to work to improve our mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Moving forward, the Youth Mental Well-being Network will be transiting to a wider remit to expand the focus of engagement beyond youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The new Network will be supported by MCCY and advised by the Interagency Taskforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Alvin Tan will share more about this initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: During the pandemic, we saw an increase in the demand for mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Planning has started to future-proof more hospital capacity for psychiatric services beyond the Institute of Mental Health (IMH), our main psychiatric hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes inpatient beds for acute and sub-acute psychiatric care and rehabilitation, as well as services such as Medical Psychiatry, Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, and Psychogeriatrics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, the National Addictions Management Service currently at IMH will be extended to other hospitals, including Changi General Hospital and National University Hospital, to make the service more accessible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mental health care services need to be more accessible and delivered in many settings, other than only in IMH, as well as integrated into the community and general medical services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The new unit at Alexandra Hospital and the provision of new services in other centres will increase the outreach of mental health care and improve the care of patients and the support to their families.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will extend this approach to social service organisations and other partners working in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To better support persons experiencing a mental health crisis such as self-harm, IMH has piloted a Crisis Response Team to respond to calls from the Singapore Police Force on cases of attempted suicide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This multi-disciplinary team will conduct an on-site assessment of the suicidal individual and provide appropriate intervention and follow-up management after the immediate crisis is resolved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Some youths who are hospitalised for risk of suicide or severe self-harm may require post-discharge residential care to allow for space and time to integrate back into the community in a more gradual way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH will be developing a new intermediate residential facility to address this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will add another therapeutic environment – not acute hospital care, not quite a community – for young patients and a new range of possible support services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about the cost of mental healthcare services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This includes consultations with psychologists providing services to CDMP providers accredited in giving mental healthcare.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The work of the Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being is the latest.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I hope Members can see that our approach will be comprehensive and holistic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will be considering a range of challenges from prevention upstream to how to deal with acute, severe illnesses, where time is of the essence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also take a good look at facilities, skills and processes, all the way from the community, a new residential centre and the acute services within the hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will do this work together with the many professionals and voluntary community organisations that have stepped up an extraordinary mental healthcare response to the challenges of the pandemic, for which I thank them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will ensure that the lessons learnt become institutionalised and sustainable to benefit our collective mental health for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If I may then, Sir, turn to a different issue – technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In response to Ms Mariam Jaafar, as we move to more telehealth solutions and a paper light environment with electronic medical records, clinical staff will receive training and orientation for new workflows.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng that we should continue to better leverage technology in healthcare delivery and our efforts have accelerated during the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, telehealth, virtual ward programmes, the use of chatbots, messaging, video or phone calls to interact with patients, so that they can recover at home instead of in the hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will provide updates on this in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In response to Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Yip Hon Weng, similar technology is also being used to help patients manage chronic conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, the Primary Tech Enhanced Care (PTEC) Home Blood Pressure Monitoring programme at selected polyclinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It could enable the earlier detection of dementia among seniors who are at high risk of the disease.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Many of our seniors with dementia and their caregivers are not aware of the condition until a more advanced stage of the disease, missing the opportunity for early intervention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is in part because early symptoms can be subtle and require specialised assessments by a trained healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital, taking up to two hours sometimes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It uses shapes and symbols and is not affected by which language the patient prefers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Artificial Intelligence is used to analyse how these shapes and symbols are being drawn.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The process is simple and can be administered by non-clinical staff and volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More seniors who are at risk could benefit from earlier diagnosis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This project is still in the research phase, but it represents some of the ways in which we are using technology and local clinical expertise to address the health problems we will face in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We share Dr Tan Wu Meng’s view that technology must enable our healthcare workforce to deliver better care to patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Good IT user interfaces can indeed improve ease of use and productivity, if they are well-integrated with data systems and clinical workflows.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The user experience as well as the manpower and time savings are important considerations when we enhance or roll out new healthcare IT systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We currently either procure or build our platforms, depending on the availability of ready solutions in the market that meet our needs, at an appropriate price point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Even as we digitalise, we agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng on the importance of protecting and securing systems and data.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH has addressed all the Committee of Inquiry (COI) recommendations arising from the SingHealth incident and learnt from them to improve our cybersecurity defences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We would like to assure Mr Leon Perera that we are actively managing healthcare capacity for future challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This year, the new National Cancer Centre Singapore (NCCS) and Sembawang Polyclinic are on track to open.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Preparation works for the redevelopment of Alexandra Hospital and the new Eastern Integrated Health Campus at Bedok North have also started.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, the Woodlands Health Campus (WHC) and the TTSH-Integrated Care Hub (ICH) are scheduled to open progressively from 2023.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The existing Queenstown Polyclinic will also be redeveloped by the end of the decade.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For dental health, we are expanding and upgrading our specialty centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The new National Dental Centre will be expanded as part of the overall Outram Campus plan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The National University Hospital Dental Centre has started accepting specialty referrals and the new National University Centre for Oral Health has started operations from 7 January 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The number of dental specialists in our public health care clusters has risen by 9% per annum from 2017 to 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Edward Chia asked about a sustainable renal treatment strategy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The emphasis should be on the upstream prevention of chronic diseases, through screening for diabetes and hypertension, and promoting healthier lifestyle interventions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH has also taken steps to provide better access and integration of care for dialysis patients through the co-location of renal dialysis centres with polyclinics and community hospitals and will continue to do so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In addition, we are encouraging the use of peritoneal dialysis which can be administered at home by the patients themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On a personal note, I would also like to record my heartfelt appreciation to those healthcare workers across our institutions that I have had the privilege to work with personally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: My colleagues, my students, most of all, my teachers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Curing the sick, relieving suffering, easing our pain and fears and helping all of us to prevent disease and stay healthy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With that, Sir, I wish you and all Singaporeans good health.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, today, I will address the challenges faced by our healthcare workers, especially during the pandemic and outline MOH’s longer term efforts to take care of our healthcare workers’ well-being and professional development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Even before the pandemic, an ageing population and increased burden of chronic diseases have placed an increased demand for more healthcare manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We factored these needs into our manpower plans and recruitment initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We had to adjust our manpower deployment during the pandemic to meet evolving needs such as the migrant worker dormitory outbreak, as well as swab and vaccination operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This would enable us to stretch our ICUs temporarily if needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Thankfully, our ICU capacity is able to cope with the current surge and patients requiring ICU care are a fraction of what we had during the Delta wave.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nonetheless we will continue make the necessary contingency plans given how unpredictable the pandemic has been.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But the pandemic had caused a sudden surge in workload and severely stretched our healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We reprioritised workload and reduced non-essential elective treatments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Absenteeism rates have stayed low, below 10% so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Not only have we stretched the public healthcare sector, but those in the private sector stepped forward to help in so many ways, including support from nursing and other healthcare students, as well as SAF.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Many have gone beyond their call of duty and we owe them a debt of gratitude.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In spite of COVID-19, we have persisted with actively recruiting for our healthcare workforce from both local and international sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To address Mr Pritam Singh and Dr Shahira Abdullah’s concerns about attrition, MOH had previously shared that the average attrition rate of doctors and nurses from public acute hospitals in 2020 and 2021 combined together was comparable with that in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Specifically, the attrition in our public healthcare workforce was 9.6% in 2019 and it dipped to 6.8% in 2020 at the height of the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This then accumulated, resulting in a rise in 2021 with a 9.8% overall attrition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But this is rather similar to our 9.6% in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Specifically, for the acute public hospitals, the average attrition in the period 2020 to 2021 was about 7% to 9% for nurses and about 3% to 5% for doctors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Understandably, some left due to family and personal reasons as the COVID-19 travel restrictions had stopped them from being able to visit and be with their loved ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But our healthcare workers have stood their post.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They have not abandoned their fight against COVID-19 and we thank them for the commitment and the steadfast efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Having said that, this does not mean that we dismiss the concerns of attrition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will still need to do more to tackle our growing manpower needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Given our low birth rate and shrinking local workforce, there are just not enough Singaporeans to meet all our healthcare manpower needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As many Members, including Ms Mariam Jaafar, have pointed out, we will need a combination of approaches to ensure an adequate and strong healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, we must ensure adequate local training pipelines and continue to attract and enable more mid-career locals to enter the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our intakes for healthcare programmes at the Institutes of Higher Learning have increased over the past five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The healthcare Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs) enables mid-career locals to acquire relevant training to join the healthcare sector as nurses and Allied Health Professionals (AHPs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: An average of around 180 mid-career locals per year entered training between 2019 and 2021 amid COVID-19, higher than the average of 110 per year between 2016 and 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will regularly review remuneration, to ensure that we continue to attract and retain staff and maintain market competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We last enhanced the salaries of selected groups of doctors and dentists in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked that we do a deep review of salaries for nurses and allied health professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, we enhanced the salaries of nurses, allied health professionals, pharmacists and allied admin staff in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And there is a second tranche of increases for nurses this year, 2022.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to monitor and review salary benchmarks in a timely manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But with a tightening workforce situation here in Singapore, we will have to accept that there will continue to be a need to hire foreign healthcare manpower to complement our local workforce and meet the needs of our ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, I thank the Leader of the Opposition Mr Pritam Singh for supporting the need for us to hire more foreign manpower to support our healthcare needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are also looking on retaining foreign nurses, including keeping their remuneration competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have also worked with other agencies on factors that are important for their retention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also need to look beyond manpower to ensure our resources are optimised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This includes further leveraging technology to extend the capabilities of our healthcare workers and innovating the way we deliver care and services and redesign healthcare jobs along with training and development opportunities so that each category of staff can perform at the top of their licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This includes training for digitalisation for healthcare professionals to be prepared for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For example, NUS has a Nursing Informatics course to equip nurses with the knowledge on the development, analysis and evaluation of information systems augmented by technologies that support, enhance and manage patient care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also continue with our job redesign efforts in introducing new role and new breeds of staff such as Care Support Associates (CSAs) that blend clinical support, administrative and operations responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will also change our care models to ensure efficient and effective delivery of appropriate care at all care settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This includes making sure we right-site patients to ensure that our resources are optimised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But there will never be enough manpower if we do not empower ourselves to improve our own health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, through preventive health, population health, Healthier SG, as Minister Ong will address later, we will also reduce the load on our overall healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To Ms Mariam Jaafar's point about organisational enablers, we agree that this is important and thus, as part of population health, we will be aligning incentives and KPIs with public healthcare clusters in how we design our programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: All these measures are in progress and will take some time to bear fruit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But there are also immediate pressures that we need to resolve and support our healthcare workers straining under the burden.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The COVID-19 restrictions on healthcare workers intermingling to bond and destress has led to a sense of isolation among healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, I want to assure Dr Shahira, Mr Leon Perera, Mr Abdul Samad and Dr Wan Rizal that staff well-being and morale is an important priority for us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: MOH had set up a cross-cluster Staff Well-being Committee in 2019 to improve the well-being of staff and to minimise burnout.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: All three public healthcare clusters also provide their staff with counselling services, helplines and peer support networks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also agree with Ms Mariam Jaafar's feedback that clusters ought to continue to induct a diverse range of talents and skillsets in their talent development and leadership pipeline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As highlighted by Dr Tan Wu Meng, one specific group of concern are the junior doctors who had to do long shifts on night calls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is benchmarked against the USA’s Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education’s (ACGME) guidelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This could be due to the nature of clinical work in certain departments or exigencies of service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This entails doctors taking turns to work night shifts for a few days at stretch without covering the daytime work, whilst others work the day shifts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Doctors may feel more refreshed when they start their night shifts with a full day’s rest, although there are possible trade-offs in requiring more manpower to do a shift system, more hand-off between team members, which carries some risk of omission in tasks, and possibly reduced learning experience as they may not follow-through in the entire care process to see how their patients progress over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It would be useful in disciplines where doctors on night duties have fewer opportunities to rest, such as Internal Medicine or General Surgery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The system has been tried in two large departments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Plans to trial this in smaller departments, unfortunately, were curtailed due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As we look at the issue of work hours, let us not lose sight of these important considerations which are inherent in the nature of our work as doctors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With shorter working hours in a week, a junior doctor may have to undergo a longer apprenticeship to acquire the necessary competencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But we also recognise that the workload and the nature of clinical work today is different from yester-years, a point which Dr Tan Wu Meng has made, with an ageing population and higher chronic disease incidence, and expectations of more collaborative and consultative care from patients and their families, the nature of clinic work has changed for our junior doctors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The stresses faced by junior doctors today are symptomatic of a wider need for transformation in the current care delivery arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Whether it is 24-hour or 30-hour shifts, what is clear is that we should not stretch our junior doctors beyond what is physiologically possible and what would risk compromising patient safety, a point also highlighted by Dr Tan Wu Meng.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But I want to caution that a simplistic framing of the issue as just work hours is not diagnosing the root cause of the problem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Recently, I met with junior doctors from the Singapore Medical Association’s (SMA) Doctors-in-Training Committee and other groups of junior doctors from all three healthcare clusters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They were proactive in sharing best practices on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We had a candid discussion on the challenges they faced, particularly in this COVID-19 period, as well as the trade-offs of possible junior doctor workflow changes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Co-led by senior doctors from all three healthcare clusters and MOH, we aim to review and recommend changes to existing healthcare practices and guidelines to improve and ensure the well-being of junior doctors, in three main areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: First, a review of junior doctor workflow models and work hour norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Other than the considerations I shared earlier, the review will also have to be done carefully as it will have an impact on the workflow of other healthcare workers who work alongside our junior doctors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another area will be to look at the fundamental balance between training and service workload, and transforming our manpower model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It would not be sustainable for us to just simply increase the "flow" of trainees going through the system to meet service demands, as this will eventually lead to a large "stock" of doctors and cause an oversupply later on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Instead, we need to raise the importance and attractiveness of work roles that are core to the service workload.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The second area of focus is career development and training of our junior doctors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Traditional specialist-focused residency programmes are not the only desirable career pathways and there is a need for stronger broad-based generalist paths such as family medicine and hospital clinicians, which if successfully implemented may also address the issue of care-fragmentation across multi-specialty teams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: One such pathway is the Hospital Clinician track we launched in 2020, which we hope to expand significantly in the years to come.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A third area of focus for this Committee will be on working with key stakeholders to promote a more inclusive culture where junior doctors can feel safe in speaking out on matters related to their safety and wellness, and importantly, to co-create policies and solutions at both the institutional and national level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We recognise that our healthcare workers have always gone above and beyond, especially during these trying times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Abdul Samad and Dr Tan Wu Meng would also be pleased to know that MOH has extended the COVID-19 Healthcare Award not just to healthcare staff in public institutions, but also to outsourced staff.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This includes cleaners and security officers, who were directly contracted by the public health institutions and publicly funded Community Care Organisations (CCOs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Paramedics under SCDF would be recognised in their own way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But the biggest encouragement for our healthcare workers must come from the support and appreciation from Singaporeans-at-large whom they serve.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We read about spontaneous ground-up actions from Singaporeans to encourage and thank our healthcare workers; examples which were cited by Mr Abdul Samad.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Unfortunately, COVID-19 has also brought out some bad behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have read about the cases of abuse and harassment towards our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The perpetuators have been taken to task and convicted by the Courts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Sadly, the number of cases has been on the rise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The actual number may be higher, as many healthcare workers exercise empathy and, therefore, do not always take a legalistic approach, and report and escalate every altercation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: However, their compassion should not be misconstrued as an acceptance to abuse or harassment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We need to make sure that our healthcare workers feel safe in their work environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I agree with Dr Tan Yia Swam that we need to recognise such abuse and institute safe reporting systems and clear penalties on offending parties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Under the Protection from Harassment Act (POHA), public healthcare workers are accorded enhanced protections under section 6 if abused or harassed while carrying out duties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Aside from legislation, we should look at other ways to deter abuse and harassment and move more upstream.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Healthcare workers should have the assurance that their employer and the healthcare system have their back, while providing them with the training to handle situations where compassion and empathy are tested to the limits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: With representatives from MOH, the Healthcare Services Employees’ Union, public healthcare clusters, community care partners and private healthcare providers, the workgroup aims to spearhead a coordinated national effort to prevent abuse and harassment of healthcare workers in the public, private and community care sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our healthcare workers should feel safe to be able and to call out abuse to allow them to focus their energies with the right frame of mind on doing their best for their patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will strengthen our private sector partnerships to meet our growing healthcare needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Dr Tan Yia Swam raised the need to have stronger oversight over business practices and medical middlemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, Third Party Administrators (TPAs) and concierge services are not regulated under the Private Hospitals and Medical Clinics Act (PHMCA) or the Healthcare Services Act (HCSA), which focuses on regulating direct service provision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Nevertheless, the Singapore Medical Council's Ethical Code and Ethical Guidelines (SMC ECEG) guide that medical practitioners contracting with TPAs should ensure they remain objective in their clinical judgement, provide the required standard of care and reflect their fees fairly and transparently to the patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: MOH will continue to monitor patient safety risks and study the evolving landscape of these TPA companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will examine how the TPA market will need to be reshaped as we make bigger shifts in preventive healthcare beyond healthcare to health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To enable even greater patient choice and better continuity of care, the MHIC is considering if doctors who are already with an IP panel can be recognised by other IP insurers to some extent, as Dr Tan Wu Meng has suggested.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will announce more details in the coming months.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Regarding access to treatments, our Free Trade Agreements and Intellectual Property obligations provide due recognition to investments that patent proprietors make in developing pharmaceutical products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is not only fair, but also ensures that Singapore remains an attractive location for drug manufacturing, research and innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Having said that, we are working with relevant Government agencies to ensure that generic drugs are not unduly delayed or obstructed from entering the Singapore market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: MOH will also continue to strengthen our position as a biomedical hub and anchor our domestic capabilities in new technologies, such as cell-based therapy, and strengthen the resilience of our healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, in today's speech, I spoke extensively about our healthcare workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To our healthcare fraternity, I know many of you may have felt exhausted and demoralised, especially in the last two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Take heart – Singaporeans are appreciative of your steadfast commitment and dedication.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: MOH is undertaking reviews to introduce structural changes in our healthcare system and manpower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We seek your patience as we work with the healthcare clusters to engage you on improving the situation on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Let us uphold the values of the healthcare profession to provide the best care we can for our patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Indeed, patients must be at the heart of all we do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Let us all, Singaporeans, help them to take better care of us.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, families form the bedrock of our society.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Since our Independence till today, they have been our first line of support, crisis after crisis.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During the pandemic, families have been a key pillar of strength, supporting each other through the ups and downs, in many ways that we, the Government, can never replace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the decades, we have strengthened our policies to support the building of strong and resilient families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At MOH, we are fully committed to this mission.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One way that we are doing so is by making Singapore a great place to raise families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And we will do so by building a more integrated social-health ecosystem for our next generation – our young.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This support will be anchored in the community, close to our homes and, most importantly, anchored around the family.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our starting point is to give every child a good start in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This also means enabling parents to raise healthy, happy and able children, who can reach their fullest potential in life.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MOH has been building an integrated ecosystem to support children and their families, across the health, social and education domains.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling and Dr Wan Rizal asked for an update and how we were addressing the health needs and risk factors of mother and child.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the past year, the task force has focused our efforts along three main thrusts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we have reviewed evidence-based research findings and are translating them into policies and programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will enable us to effectively address the health needs, risk factors and the wider health determinants across the developmental stages of a child, starting as early as pre-conception to adolescence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we have reviewed the current model of service delivery for children and their families, with the aim to improve accessibility to services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We engaged a wide range of stakeholders on how we could strengthen support for them.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This included parents, grandparents, caregivers and professionals from the healthcare, education and social service sectors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, we reviewed how we communicated and engaged these stakeholders because we wanted to know what mattered most to them and to ensure that our messages and support to them remained relevant.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I am glad to share that we have completed the first phase of review and planning.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue further cross-domain and cross-agency discussions over the next year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Allow me to elaborate on two cross-agency initiatives that we will be rolling out from this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To build strong and resilient families, we need to ensure that parents can get timely access to health services so that they are healthy and able to take care of their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We recognise the challenges that many parents face.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They are often stretched for time, having to balance multiple roles, both in the family and at the workplace.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is an area where we could better integrate services so both parents and child can receive support concurrently without making multiple trips.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Families can access integrated services, such as vaccination, childhood developmental and postnatal depression screenings and breastfeeding support services concurrently, for both mother and child.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: She had brought her nine-month-old son to Punggol polyclinic for his vaccinations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the same time, the care team at the Integrated Maternal and Child Wellness Hub provided her with detailed guidance on what to expect at each stage of her son's development, for example, the types of food and developmental activities that may be appropriate at different stages.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through their support, she and her husband have developed better knowledge and are more confident in caring for their newborn.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We want more children and their families to benefit from this service.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It actively identifies and supports young children under three years old from low-income families living in rental flats, to address potential health risks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under this initiative, the children will be systematically screened for both health and social needs, when they visit the polyclinic for their regular check-ups, such as vaccination or childhood developmental screening, for example, whether the child's family may be facing any financial difficulties that could impact their health and well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The EMBRACEPLUS team will also work closely with social and community agencies, including practitioners from KidSTART.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This ensures that their needs are holistically supported.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Next, we want to take integration a step further and will do so across the health and social domains so that we can provide for our mother-child dyad, beyond just physical well-being and those with complex care needs like the EMBRACEPLUS.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They can assist families with accessing other relevant programmes by our community partners.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will also explore the use of virtual access to services to enhance convenience.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our support for families and their children must also be holistic and comprehensive.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior Minister of State Janil has shared on initiatives to promote mental well-being and improve lifestyle habits and Parliamentary Secretary Rahayu will elaborate on our public education efforts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In closing, together with the support of Singaporeans, community partners and Government agencies, we will continue to strengthen support for families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will anchor care and support for our young and their families in the community and, most importantly, around the family, because we want Singapore to be a great place for families to thrive and flourish.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, preventive health is an important part of ensuring overall health and well-being.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Good preventive health will lead to lower health risks, earlier detection and management of diseases, as well as longer-term sustainability of our healthcare system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support good preventive health, we constantly evolve and adjust our approach to build a healthy ecosystem for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In response to Ms Ng Ling Ling's question on how we encourage individuals to take ownership of their health, we do so by making it easier to adopt and prioritise healthy living and bring more lifestyle programmes closer to our residents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our efforts can only succeed with strong participation of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Today, I seek the continued support of Singaporeans as I share our upcoming efforts to collectively nudge the community towards healthier ways of life and strengthening support for women, seniors and their families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Key components of a healthy lifestyle include good nutrition and diet as well as sufficient physical activity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We actively encourage Singaporeans to adopt a healthier diet, particularly for sugar and sodium consumption.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about the War on Diabetes, which we declared in 2016.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In 2019, MOH announced plans to introduce regulatory measures for beverages high in sugar content.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Health Promotion Board (HPB) also extended the Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme (HIDS) in 2018 to support the development and commercialisation of lower-sugar products.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As of December 2021, seven beverage suppliers were on board the scheme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Through these efforts and support from the industry, we have observed early success with the industry accelerating the reformulation of sweetened beverages.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singaporeans can now choose from a larger variety of healthier drinks.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To further reduce the intake of sugar, MOH also announced in 2020 that the labelling and advertising measures for sugar will be extended to freshly prepared beverages.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB has conducted an implementation consultation with the industry on the proposed specification.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: More details of the measures will be released when ready.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Together with public education, we will continue to explore using regulation and industry support to make healthier ingredients and foods easily accessible to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng will also be pleased to know that we will be doing more to reduce Singaporeans’ sodium consumption.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is almost double that of World Health Organization’s recommended limit, translating to more than 1.5 teaspoons of salt daily.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: High sodium intake is associated with increased risk of hypertension, which is in turn associated with higher risks of stroke and heart attack.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The National Population Health Survey revealed that slightly more than one in three Singapore residents aged 18 to 74 had hypertension during the period 2019 to 2020.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is a significant increase from 2017 and reminds Singaporeans of the need to adopt better dietary practices.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will introduce a three-pronged strategy to reduce sodium consumption.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will increase support through HIDS to shift the food service sector towards using lower-sodium alternatives such as lower-sodium salt, which contains about 30% less sodium compared to regular salt at the same quantity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Second, increasing the range and variety of lower-sodium salt, sauces and seasonings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB will work with major salt suppliers and retailers to expand the range of lower-sodium salt.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will also ramp up existing efforts using HIDS to spur reformulation of lower-sodium sauces and seasonings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB will launch a multi-year nationwide campaign to raise awareness of the effects of overconsuming salt in our diet and educate the public on available alternatives and ways to replace salt without compromising on taste.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Sufficient physical activity is also important for a healthy lifestyle.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are various efforts to support Singaporeans to exercise.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, the National Steps ChallengeTM continued amid COVID-19 and is now in its sixth season.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Additionally, HPB’s leisure-time physical activity programmes such as mall workouts at health promoting malls, Sundays at the Park, Community Physical Activity Programme are still available where possible, in line with prevailing safe management measures.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Where feasible, some on-ground programmes are taken virtually, for participants who work from home or prefer to work out remotely or individually to keep active.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Another area of concern impacting healthy living is smoking.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Tobacco use is the single greatest cause of preventable death globally.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: About 10.1% of Singaporeans smoke daily based on results from the National Population Health Survey 2020.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In Singapore, we are committed to our long-term goal of bringing the overall smoking rate to a level that is as low as possible.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We need to consider Singapore’s context and local trends of tobacco use in developing our tobacco control strategy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Globally, there is an increasing trend of smokers using vapourisers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes increasing education on the harms of vaping, enhancing the penalty framework for vaping and better whole-of-Government coordination in preventing smuggling and illicit sale and use of vapourisers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support smokers who wish to kick their smoking habits, we previously announced plans to provide subsidies under new tobacco cessation pilots at public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am pleased to share that we have received proposals from our healthcare institutions and are evaluating them closely.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Concurrently, we will continue to strengthen our existing multi-front approach to curb tobacco consumption and vaping.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With a healthy diet, active and smoke-free lifestyle, we can all live better.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To help us make timely adjustments to our lifestyle behaviours and seek treatment early if needed, I encourage Singaporeans to seek appropriate, evidence-based health screening.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Chronic disease screening participation rates had hovered around 63% to 66% from 2017 to 2020.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We note Dr Lim Wee Kiak’s interest in health screening.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will be doing more to increase take-up, such as working with partners to further encourage the use of Screen for Life, a national health screening programme that provides heavily subsidised chronic disease and cancer screenings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Dr Lim Wee Kiak pointed out, immunisations are important to protect ourselves against vaccine-preventable diseases.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The National Adult Immunisation Schedule (NAIS) was introduced in November 2017 to provide national-level guidance on important vaccinations for persons aged 18 and older.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH actively works with our primary care partners and other stakeholders such as HPB to increase uptake of these nationally recommended vaccinations, especially among seniors for influenza and pneumococcal vaccinations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We urge Singaporeans to proactively find out more and take up these vaccinations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support everyone to be as healthy as possible, we also cannot adopt a one-size-fits-all approach, as everyone faces different risks and challenges.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our health promotion efforts are inclusive to all and targeted efforts taking into consideration different backgrounds and cultural preferences are layered on for select groups to increase their access to healthy living resources.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB’s Healthy Living Passport programme was piloted with about 50 families last year to serve the needs of our lower-income families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Activities that parents and children engage in include planning for healthier and economical meals as well as games emphasising the importance of parent-child communication and a balance of physical activities with age-appropriate use of smart devices.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Volunteers who befriend the families also participate in the programmes and continue to provide health tips based on the families’ needs after the programme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB will be reaching out to more families this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In Malay):   Dr Wan Rizal asked about outreach efforts to our minority communities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Last year, I shared plans to form a new workgroup aimed at strengthening health efforts for the Malay community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: After identifying the key issues that should be given attention, HPB has brought together community leaders with the experience and expertise to form a Malay Community Outreach workgroup, or MCO.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Under MCO, there are five new sub-committees focusing on mental well-being, reducing smoking, improving dietary habits, increasing physical activity and health screening within the Malay community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MCO will work with various parties to expand the reach of successful HPB programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, HPB collaborated with M3, the Malay Activity Executive Committees (MAECs) and mosques to organise online wellness workshops for more than 200 Malay residents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This year, HPB will expand its reach by working with all MAECs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To encourage healthier eating habits within the Malay community in the month of Ramadan, HPB partnered with MAECs, Mendaki, mosques and Malay-Muslim organisations, such as the Tabung Amal Aidilfitri Trust Fund and Perdaus to distribute healthier groceries to more than 24,500 Malay families.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will work with more MAECs, mosques and Malay-Muslim bodies to promote healthier eating habits during the month of Ramadan this year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Azrin has served the Marsiling MAEC for more than 10 years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As chairman of Marsiling MAEC, he works actively with HPB and other partners to organise various activities that cater to residents’ needs, such as health talks and screenings.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: During Ramadan last year, he helped HPB to distribute healthy grocery packs to low-income families and encouraged them to choose healthier food during the festive period.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As the Vice-Chairman of An-Nur Mosque, he also onboarded the mosque on the Jaga Kesihatan, Jaga Ummah (Taking Care of Health, Taking Care of Community - JKJU) initiative.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Azrin also practises what he preaches daily.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: He and his family stay active by walking and cycling, and chooses healthier products that carry the Healthier Choice Symbol when buying groceries.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: May Mr Azrin's efforts inspire the community to lead a healthier lifestyle.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: (In English): Similarly, HPB also considers cultural sensitivities and partners stakeholders to implement health promotion activities for the Indian Community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, HPB has been working with key stakeholders like the Singapore Indian Development Association (SINDA) to tap on their programmes and culturally significant events such as Deepavali to reinforce healthy cooking and eating as a family.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB also actively engages Indian food and beverage outlets to participate in the Healthier Dining Programme, which provides and rewards customers for selecting healthier options.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
